episodes.title: Trump's Mission to Get Jensen Huang Back at Nvidia
episodes.about: Nvidia shocked the world this morning when it announced it would be reinstating Jensen Huang as its chief executive. Guest host Max Read called two reporters to make sense of the news: Stephen Witt, who wrote a biography of Jensen Huang called "The Thinking Machine," and Jonathan Swan, a White House reporter for The New York Times. They break down how it happened — and what to expect next.
episodes.why: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO this morning; guest host Max Read talks to his biographer Stephen Witt and White House reporter Jonathan Swan about how it happened and what comes next.

episodes.title: When AI Labs Rival Nations
episodes.about: Anthropic's IPO has united AI safety advocates and accelerationists around an unlikely concern. If a company gains the kind of influence we associate with a government, what does it owe the public? This Long Read Sunday explores the debate over Anthropic's power, why some in tech would welcome handing control to AI, and what happens when businesses give agents a goal and let them decide how to reach it.
episodes.why: Anthropic's IPO has safety advocates and accelerationists asking the same question: when a lab carries government-level influence, what does it owe the public?

episodes.title: What happens if AI becomes its own successor?
episodes.about: A new report from the AI safety non-profit METR has a lot of AI insiders warning about something called recursive self-improvement or RSI — where AI sort of builds itself, leading to a rapid explosion in capabilities. Rachel Steratore, a senior researcher at RAND, says now is the time to prepare.
episodes.why: A new METR report has insiders warning about recursive self-improvement — AI building itself toward a rapid capability jump; RAND's Rachel Steratore says now is the time to prepare. Eleven minutes.

episodes.title: The ‘Everywhere, All at Once’ Cybersecurity Crisis
episodes.about: It's been called a lot of names: “black October,” “bugmageddon,” “the patchpocalypse,” “a new dark age,” “software Beirut.” Artificial intelligence has thrown us into a new era of digital insecurity, exposing bugs in the foundations of our digital infrastructure, supercharging the capabilities of hackers, and sending companies and governments scrambling in response. The recent outages at the Federal Aviation Administration, Microsoft Outlook, Apple iCloud and Chase bank branches all appear to be part of the story.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — The Ezra Klein Show is the New York Times interview show, new to this list; cybersecurity reporter Nicole Perlroth on how AI supercharged hackers and exposed bugs in the foundations of the internet.

episodes.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
episodes.about: Hayden Field, The Verge's senior AI reporter, joins Nilay Patel to discuss the Anthropic IPO in the third and final episode of Decoder's series about AI in real life. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders.
episodes.why: The Verge's Hayden Field on whether Anthropic can keep putting money into safety now that public shareholders own a piece of it — the close of Decoder's AI-in-real-life series.
